newsitem.title: HUNGARY: BUDAPEST AIRPORT TERMINAL TO FOCUS ON CARGO BIZ.
newsitem.headline: BUDAPEST AIRPORT TERMINAL TO FOCUS ON CARGO BIZ.

text.p: Hungary's Air Traffic and Airport Adminstration (LRI) said on Friday it planned to invest roughly $30 million to renovate Terminal One at Budapest Ferihegy Airport to serve non-commercial passenger flights, mainly cargo and courrier traffic.

"The cost will be around $30 million," Jozsef Farkas, LRI's investment director, told Reuters. "We have no details on the exact costs, but we will start preparing a plan for the project by the end of 1997."
The renovation, scheduled for completion by 2000, will enable Terminal One to handle all of the airport's cargo-only charter, courier, general aviation and governmental flights, Farkas said.
General aviation flights carry a maximum of 10 passengers, who are not required to buy tickets, he said.
The renovation is expected to start in September 1998, when a $120 million expansion of Terminal Two is scheduled for completion, Farkas said.
The enlarged Terminal Two, which opened in 1985, will handle all commercial passenger flights. Terminal One opened in 1950.
Both terminals now share cargo and passenger traffic.
